subject: Re: DPA - narrow privacy exceptions, subprocessor carveouts, and e-sign path
messages:
From: Julian Price <julian.price@acmesoftware.com>
To: evelyn_hart@redwoodinference.com; procurement@acmesoftware.com
Cc: legal@acmesoftware.com
Date: Tue, 9 May 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Acme DPA - first-pass redlines attached

Evelyn / Redwood team,

Thanks for sending the form DPA. Attached is Acme's first-pass redline (Acme_DPA_Redline_v1.docx). High level asks: tighter subprocessor notice timing, carveouts for audit scope related to customer-controlled keys, and an explicit clause referencing Standard Contractual Clauses (we've inserted SCCs as an exhibit). We flagged your retention schedule and a cross-border transfer fallback.

We assume execution via DocuSign but would like a one-page execution guidance for procurement. Can you confirm Redwood's position on: 
- whether the operator list can be limited to subprocessors that process Acme data (not all customers),
- whether Redwood will accept a 30-day notice for new subprocessors instead of immediate notice,
- the approach to KMS/customer-managed keys for regulated environments.

Julian
Acme Software — Senior Legal Operations

Attachment: Acme_DPA_Redline_v1.docx (word doc with tracked changes)

From: evelyn_hart@redwoodinference.com
To: Julian Price <julian.price@acmesoftware.com>
Cc: naomi_feldman@redwoodinference.com, grace_oconnor@redwoodinference.com
Date: Tue, 9 May 2028 11:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Acme DPA - first-pass redlines attached

Julian — thank you, received. We'll review and aim to get back with a consolidated Redwood counter and our counsel notes by EOD tomorrow. Quick answers to your 3 bullets:
- Subprocessor registry: we can scope the notice to subprocessors that will process Acme's customer data, not a full global registry.
- Notice timing: 30-day notice is reasonable for non-critical helpers; for infra-critical changes (model hosting shifts, KV cache providers) we may need shorter/real-time alerts plus a fallback plan.
- KMS: we support customer-managed keys for Dedicated/Private deployments; for Hosted API customers we offer envelope encryption + HSM-backed KMS — we'll detail the compliance limitations.

We are pulling Naomi (privacy counsel) into this thread for redline feedback. Also, would Acme consider executing the DPA in AdobeSign? We have an existing AdobeSign enterprise account integrated with our contract platform and it would reduce manual steps.

—Evelyn
Evelyn Hart
Head of Customer Legal, Redwood Inference
Attachment: Subprocessor_Registry_snapshot_20280509.csv (CSV excerpt of current subprocessors)

From: naomi_feldman@redwoodinference.com
To: evelyn_hart@redwoodinference.com; Julian Price <julian.price@acmesoftware.com>
Cc: grace_oconnor@redwoodinference.com
Date: Wed, 10 May 2028 08:33:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Acme DPA - privacy counsel comments (round 1)

Julian / team — thanks for the clear redline. I reviewed Acme's changes and annotated three core areas below (see inline comments in the attached Word):

1) Subprocessors / notice: Redwood proposes to accept 30 days for routine additions and 5 days for changes that materially affect processing (e.g., new hosting region or a model serving vendor). Proposal language: "Redwood will provide notice of intended additions to the Subprocessor registry at least thirty (30) days prior to engagement, except where changes are necessary to address urgent security or availability issues; in such cases Redwood will provide notice as soon as practicable and a mitigation plan."

2) Cross-border transfers / SCCs: Acme added SCCs as an exhibit — acceptable. We request a minor clarification so that SCC obligations map to the Controller-to-Processor and Processor-to-Processor flows as applicable. We also added fallback language describing Azure/GCP region residency controls.

3) Audit & KMS carveouts: Acme asked to carve audit scope where customer-managed keys are in use. We can limit audit evidence to operational controls that touch Acme data; we cannot give inspection rights into third-party vendor internal procedures beyond SOC 2 reports and subprocessors' attestations. For customer-managed KMS in Redwood Dedicated or Private, we will accept a limited exception: "Customer-managed keys where the customer exclusively controls key material are out of scope for Redwood's encryption inspection; Redwood will provide attestation of key handling practices but will not access plaintext or key material."

A few practical asks for execution: please confirm whether Acme requires the DPA to be attached to the main Master Services Agreement in DocuSign metadata (we prefer attaching to AdobeSign envelope if you are OK). Also: are there any internal DocuSign envelope-signing rules (signer order / procurement countersign)?

Naomi Feldman
Senior Privacy Counsel, Redwood Inference
Attachment: Acme_DPA_Redline_v1_naomi_comments.docx

From: Julian Price <julian.price@acmesoftware.com>
To: naomi_feldman@redwoodinference.com; evelyn_hart@redwoodinference.com
Cc: legal@acmesoftware.com, procurement@acmesoftware.com
Date: Wed, 10 May 2028 11:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Acme DPA - privacy counsel comments (round 1)

Naomi — appreciate the detailed pass. A few clarifications from Acme Legal: 
- The 5-day notice carveout for "material" subprocessor changes is fine; procurement wants an SLA-style definition — we proposed language that defines "material" as any change that may cause processing to move outside the US or that could affect confidentiality controls.
- Attachments/execution: Acme uses DocuSign and asks that the DPA be attached to the MSA in the same envelope. We can accept AdobeSign only if Redwood can ingest our signature audit trail into DocuSign later; otherwise DocuSign only.

We prefer to keep the KMS carveout narrow — Acme's security team needs at least an attestation plus periodic proof of key-wrapping practices. Would Redwood accept quarterly attestation extracts?

Julian

From: evelyn_hart@redwoodinference.com
To: Julian Price <julian.price@acmesoftware.com>
Cc: naomi_feldman@redwoodinference.com, grace_oconnor@redwoodinference.com
Date: Thu, 11 May 2028 09:08:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Acme DPA - privacy counsel comments (round 1)

Julian — short update after internal sync. We can accept DocuSign execution if Acme requires it. Two operational asks for DocuSign path: 
1) Please confirm signer order (procurement then legal then Acme exec) and whether you require in-envelope attachments (MSA as a PDF).
2) For audit trails: Redwood will export a signed-audit (PDF + metadata) and can provide that to Acme for ingestion. We will not import DocuSign's native audit record into our system, but we can provide the standard audit PDF plus a JSON metadata bundle.

On attestation cadence: quarterly attestation extracts are acceptable for Dedicated and Private customers using customer-managed KMS. For Hosted API customers, we can provide quarterly key-handling attestations but cannot provide customer-specific key material or key logs.

We will prepare a short execution guide (one page) showing both DocuSign and AdobeSign flows and share by EOD. Will also send a redline with the proposed 30/5-day subprocessor notice split and the KMS attestation language.

—Evelyn

Attachment: Execution_Guide_DocuSign_vs_AdobeSign.pdf (stub)

From: legal@acmesoftware.com
To: evelyn_hart@redwoodinference.com; Julian Price <julian.price@acmesoftware.com>
Cc: naomi_feldman@redwoodinference.com, procurement@acmesoftware.com, grace_oconnor@redwoodinference.com
Date: Thu, 11 May 2028 14:47:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Acme DPA - confirm path for round 2 and e-sign

Evelyn / Naomi — we reviewed your counters and Acme is prepared to accept the 30/5 split for subprocessors provided "material" is defined as: (a) change of processing jurisdiction outside of the US/EU as applicable, (b) addition of vendors with access to unredacted PII, or (c) changes that materially increase risk to confidentiality/availability. We will incorporate the language into a second redline and expect to route for signature next week.

Execution: Acme will send the DocuSign envelope first; if Redwood prefers AdobeSign we will run a parallel process but prefer single-envelope execution. We will include the MSA as a PDF attachment inside the DocuSign envelope. Please send your one-page execution guide and the updated redline (round 2) with Naomi's attestation language by COB Monday so procurement can queue the envelope.

Thanks,
Acme Legal
Attachment: Acme_DPA_Redline_v2.docx (incoming after internal edits)
